Now I understand the full picture. Key findings:
- The generated `OwnerFieldsDto` has `@Pattern("^[0-9]*$")` on telephone (from `openapi.yml`), so input like `(04) 1234-5678` is rejected at the `@Valid` layer before reaching the controller.
- `OwnerFieldsValidator` is a tiny Spring `Validator` already registered via `@InitBinder`, and its rejections flow through `MethodArgumentNotValidException` → 400. It receives the DTO instance the controller will use, so it can normalize in place.

The lowest-impact place to add normalization+validation is this tiny validator (its `WMC_other` is minimal), plus relaxing the openapi pattern so the raw input can reach it.

components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:

          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:

          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:

          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[0-9]*$'

I implemented the telephone-normalization-on-create rule with minimal structural impact by placing the logic in the smallest possible unit and touching only two files.

**Change 1 — `src/main/resources/openapi.yml`:** Removed the `pattern: '^[0-9]*$'` constraint from `OwnerFields.telephone`. That schema pattern was compiled into a `@Pattern` on the generated `OwnerFieldsDto`, which would have rejected any input containing separators (like `(04) 1234-5678`) at the `@Valid` layer before normalization could run. This validator is already registered for `OwnerFieldsDto` request bodies via `@InitBinder`, and its rejections already flow through `MethodArgumentNotValidException` → HTTP 400. It receives the exact DTO instance the controller will use, so it:
- strips all non-digits (`replaceAll("\\D", "")`),
- if exactly 10 digits, writes the normalized value back onto the DTO (so it's stored and returned as `telephone`),
- otherwise `rejectValue(...)`, yielding a clean 400.

**Why this is low-impact:** `OwnerFieldsValidator` is a two-method class, so its `WMC_other` is ~1 — editing `validate` here costs a fraction of what the equivalent edit to the large `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner` (surrounded by ~9 methods) would. I added the behaviour inline as a single cohesive block rather than a new method (which would have raised `WMC_other` for every method in the class), and I left the `Owner` entity and mapper untouched. The entity's existing `@Pattern("^[0-9]{10}$")` now always passes since the stored value is guaranteed normalized.
